entities.name: Augustan History
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Augustan History is a late Roman collection of biographies, written in Latin, of the Roman emperors, their junior colleagues, designated heirs, and usurpers from 117–284 AD. This vast and complex work, created by the Scriptores Historiae Augustae, presents a multifaceted portrait of the imperial era, oscillating between fact and fiction. By examining the lives and reigns of these prominent figures, historians gain insight into the intricate web of alliances, power struggles, and cultural influences that shaped the Late Roman Empire.

The Augustan History is a testament to the enduring legacy of Roman power, as it chronicles the rise and fall of dynasties, the ebb and flow of imperial fortunes, and the evolution of imperial culture. Through its pages, readers can witness the emergence of new social classes, the growth of urban centers, and the spread of Christianity throughout the Mediterranean world.

Despite its reputation for embellishments and fabrications, the Augustan History remains a vital source for understanding the complexities of Late Roman society, politics, and culture. Its authors, drawing upon a vast array of sources, including official documents, literary works, and oral traditions, offer a rich and nuanced account of this pivotal moment in human history.

The Augustan History stands as a powerful reminder of the intricate dynamics at play during the Late Roman period, a time of great upheaval, cultural transformation, and imperial grandeur. As a window into the past, it continues to captivate scholars and enthusiasts alike, offering a glimpse into the world of ancient Rome's most fascinating and enigmatic rulers.
